newsitem.title: UAE: Saudi seeks to import more gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Saudi seeks to import more gasoline.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil producer and exporter, is aiming to import more gasoline to meet the demands of two million Moslems at next month's annual pilgrimage in the kingdom, Gulf-based traders said Monday.
State-owned Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil company in terms of reserves, has issued a tender to buy 1.5 million barrels of gasoline for delivery in April, traders said.
"They probably need the barrels because of the haj (pilgrimage) ... it's building up inventory to prevent possible shortfalls," said one Saudi-based Asian oil executive.

The haj usually increases road traffic for the one million Saudis travelling to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina and another million foreign pilgrims, many of whom arrive at the commercial capital Jeddah. Mecca, one of Islam's holiest sites, is 45 miles (72 km) southeast of Jeddah, the main port of entry for most pilgrims. Medina is 257 miles (414 km) northeast of Jeddah.
The actual volume that Aramco would buy was unclear and some traders said that current strong market prices might lead the state oil firm to delay or cut back on tender purchases.
Aramco regularly imports gasoline from neighbouring Bahrain under a term contract and has also bought the occasional cargo from the spot market to cover shortfalls, traders said.

Traders said Aramco's tender, which could cost it about $45 million at current market prices, was a sign that even local production from the kingdom's eight refineries and current import levels could not satisfy rising demand in Saudi Arabia, where prices at the pump are 16 cents a litre, or about 61 cents a gallon.
"Aramco has been buying spot cargoes since the end of 1996 but this is its biggest tender to date," a Kuwait-based trader said.
